clue.text: Crowd of millions on Belarus’s western borders (3)

indicators.note: on a map west is the left-hand side, so the western border of each word is its leftmost letter

annotation.surface: A news report of a huge crowd massing at the western frontier of Belarus.
annotation.walkthrough: Belarus looks like the star of the clue, but it only supplies its first letter; 'western borders' reads as geography and means the left-hand edge of each word.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: the word names a large, unruly throng of people, usually an angry one.

clue.text: Pulp hit needs no introduction (4)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Needs no introduction' is a showbiz cliché, but here it is literal: the word for hit loses its first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: As verbs both mean crushing food or other soft material into a soft, shapeless paste.

clue.text: Licensed premises above Top Man in East London town (7)

the man at the very top of a kingdom

annotation.walkthrough: Top Man is a British high-street menswear chain, which makes the shop-above-the-pub picture plausible.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: Barking is a district in the London borough of Barking and Dagenham, east of the City.

clue.text: I’d put back vegetable juice before vegetable wine went (11)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Vegetable' appears twice and does two different jobs: first as part of 'vegetable juice', then alone.

clue.text: Done up smartly, Ant’s best man made a speech (9)

blocks.note: Ant and Dec are a British TV presenting duo; Ant's partner

annotation.walkthrough: Ant and Dec are a hugely famous British TV double act, so 'Ant's best man' is his partner, not a wedding role.
annotation.definitionFit: A room or tree trimmed with ornaments has been decked out, made to look smart and festive.

clue.text: Get to hear the first part of Carmen (3)

annotation.walkthrough: The opera setting of 'hear' and 'Carmen' hides a single letter, whose name is a word in its own right.

clue.text: Voucher from a posh dude accepted by Bill (6,5)

annotation.surface: A voucher handed over by a toff and accepted by someone called Bill.
annotation.walkthrough: Bill looks like a man's name but is a notice pasted on a wall. A postal order is a British money order bought at a post office.
annotation.definitionFit: A paper slip bought at a post office and cashed by the payee, so a kind of money voucher.

clue.text: Striking effect of knitted lace on Twiggy’s top (5)

indicators.note: knitting works strands into a new pattern, as the letters are reworked
in a down entry the first piece sits on top of the next
the top of a word in a down clue is its first letter

annotation.surface: A fashion note on the stunning look of a knitted lace top worn by Twiggy, the 1960s supermodel.
annotation.walkthrough: Twiggy was the iconic 1960s British model, so 'Twiggy's top' reads as her clothing; it is just her first letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Borrowed from French, the word means brilliant display or dazzling success that makes an impression.

clue.text: The start of Emmanuel Macron’s unconventional love affair (7)

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter
unconventional means not in the usual order, so the letters are rearranged

annotation.surface: A remark on the French president's famously unusual marriage.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface alludes to Emmanuel Macron's marriage to his former teacher, and the answer's letters are almost all in his surname.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a romantic relationship between two people, often a brief or secret one.

clue.text: District attorney starts to reflect and knowingly question something hitherto unperceived (4,6)

indicators.note: the starts of the words that follow are their first letters

blocks.note: an issue, as in 'a matter of taste'

annotation.surface: A prosecutor pausing to think and pointedly ask about something no one had noticed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'And' sits between the two words whose first letters are taken, so only 'reflect' and 'knowingly' contribute.
annotation.definitionFit: Astronomers infer this invisible mass from gravity but have never directly detected it, hence unperceived.

clue.text: Sons followed by exhausted parents with salad stuck in teeth (9)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Teeth' looks like part of the picture but is the definition; 'exhausted' means emptied, not tired.

annotation.definitionFit: Definition by origin: these primates live wild only on the island of Madagascar, so one is a Madagascan native.

clue.text: Newspaper that prompts self-reflection (6)

blocks.note: reflection taken literally: the glass that shows you your own face

annotation.surface: A paper whose articles make readers think about themselves.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Self-reflection' reads as soul-searching but is meant literally, your own image in the glass.
annotation.definitionFit: The Daily Mirror is a long-running British tabloid, and a looking glass throws back your own image.

clue.text: State in which The Departed is set (5,6)

definitions.text: State in which The Departed is set

blocks.clueFragment: State in which The Departed is set

the setter's reading: the departed are the dead, and 'set' means stiffened; the state is a bodily condition

annotation.surface: A film-trivia question about where Scorsese's The Departed takes place.
annotation.walkthrough: The Departed is a Scorsese film set in Boston, Massachusetts, so 'state' suggests a US state; read literally, the departed are the dead and 'set' means stiffened.

clue.text: Distant relative to close cycling function on the outskirts of Yarm (7)

annotation.walkthrough: 'Distant relative' looks like a far-off cousin, but the definition runs on: 'distant', relative to 'close', is its opposite.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: distant and close are words of opposite meaning, so distant stands in that relation to close.

clue.text: Olympic sport during which tension makes people jumpy (10)

annotation.definitionFit: Gymnasts bounce on a taut sprung bed in this event, which has been part of the Olympics since 2000.

clue.text: Fair, intelligent leader gets kicked out (5)

annotation.surface: A just and clever political leader is ousted anyway.
annotation.walkthrough: The political leader of the surface is simply the leading letter of the word for intelligent.

clue.text: Dopiest tigers go swimming around midnight (9)

annotation.definitionFit: Superlatives of dazed and sluggish: the most dopey person is the one most befuddled, as after sleep or drink.

clue.text: Test participant flipping second of two coins ahead of game’s opening (6,3)

the opening of a word is its first letter
